A joint operation of the People's Bank of China with Shanghai police clamped down on the Solana Accelerate China 2026 four-day tour. Authorities blocked the project's events in Shanghai, while the financial regulator in parallel launched an investigation against those locals who helped the blockchain platform with logistics and public relations.

What drew such a harsh reaction from the Chinese authorities was 'too aggressive' offline marketing of the tour. On the evening of October 14, a team associated with Solana, together with Shanghai contractors, put giant vibrant logos of the SOL token on the Citigroup Tower skyscraper facade in Lujiazui - the very heart of Shanghai's financial district. This was not just an ad: top managers, including Solana Foundation president Lily Lu, started publicly boasting about the opening of Shanghai's new office in a prestigious building.

All this massive campaign predictably caused an excitement in crypto circles. Even Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, known simply as CZ, expressed his amusement, calling 'amazing' the fact that Solana managed to not only do a promo in China, but get an office there as well. BNB Chain did not achieve such a success, added CZ.

It seems like the organizers tried to bypass the regulatory barriers using a positioning trick. The four-day tour between Shanghai, Hangzhou, Shenzhen, and Beijing was marketed strictly around technologies like AI agents, robots, IT development - not about crypto at all.

The maneuver did not get recognition in China to say the least, and the backlash did not take long to follow.

The morning session on October 16 in Shangri-La was shut down outright, with participants held for over an hour on the street after police suddenly arrived. Lily Lu tried to narrow the angles and stated that the cancellation was caused by registrations quadrupling, so the site was not ready to invite all registrants.

Fast forward to November 6 and representatives of the People's Bank of China, in an exclusive interview with the state agency Financial News, finally ended speculations on what actually happened. He directly called the skyline ad and all the aligned events an illegal marketing of virtual currencies. The Central Bank's position is 'black and white' there: SOL is a cryptocurrency and Solana's infra not only facilitates coins issuance, but also helps stablecoin turnover (especially USDT), which is banned.

Organizers in the face of Solana Foundation breached the crypto-risk agreement jointly issued back in February 2026 by eight Chinese authority departments. The document directly bans all the promotion of overseas crypto projects and implements individual liability for Chinese citizens and companies that help to do this.

Solana Foundation hasn't provided any official comments on the matter yet.

The signal by People's Bank of China is unambiguous though: full cleanup of all the mainland market out of foreign blockchain networks and activities associated with them.

Ripple received high-profile attention during the recently concluded Dubai FinTech Summit, which took place November 2-3, 2026, with Emirates Airline Chairman and Chief Executive Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum visiting the company's booth during the event.

In a recent X post about the event, Reece Merrick, Ripple's Senior Executive Officer/Managing Director, Middle East and Africa, commented that it was an incredible week at the summit. He added that it was a busy couple of days marked by immense interest and strong engagement around Ripple's offerings across the Middle East region.

What an incredible week at the @DubaiFinTechSum! A busy couple of days marked by immense interest and strong engagement around @Ripple's offerings across the region. We remain deeply committed to scaling our footprint in the Middle East out of our @DIFC hub. It was also an honor to welcome His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, the Chairman and Chief Executive of Emirates Airline, to our booth, alongside DIFC Governor, His Excellency. Merrick also noted that the company is still committed to growing its presence in the Middle East through its hub at the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC). Ripple's exhibition stand was also attended by DIFC Governor Essa Kazim and DIFC CEO Arif Amiri, as well as Emirates Airline Chairman and Chief Executive Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum.

The high-profile visit was a highlight of Ripple's presence at the summit, offering a platform to connect with regional stakeholders and demonstrate its financial technology solutions. Ripple's commitment to the Middle East as a central region for its growth strategy remains steadfast, with its presence in the DIFC serving as a springboard for fostering relationships and identifying potential opportunities within the market.

Ripple in 2026 said it was expanding in the UAE with the opening of its Middle East and Africa (MEA) regional headquarters in the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC). The announcement highlighted the strategic footprint of the firm in the country.

Solana’s price decline below $90 has put its recovery prospects at risk, but a potential bullish signal is emerging beneath the ongoing sell-off. While SOL continues to record lower lows, its RSI is moving in the opposite direction, hinting that bearish momentum may be losing strength.

At the same time, 12 consecutive sessions without net inflows into spot Solana ETFs highlight weakening institutional demand. This creates a critical battle between fading selling pressure and a lack of fresh capital. Could this RSI divergence signal Solana’s next rebound, or is another leg lower still ahead?

Solana is trading near $89.90 after breaking below an important support area. The decline follows a broader correction from its October highs, with the token continuing to form lower highs and lower lows.

The latest breakdown also reflects weakening buying interest. SOL has struggled to regain its short-term moving averages, while the broader price structure continues to favour sellers. The loss of support has further weakened the recovery attempt, leaving the token vulnerable to continued volatility.

Institutional flows are adding another layer of pressure to Solana’s recovery prospects. According to the latest market update, spot Solana ETFs have recorded no net inflows for 12 consecutive trading sessions.

JUST IN: 🇺🇸 US spot crypto ETF outflows on Nov 6.• 📉 Bitcoin ($BTC): -$412M• 📉 Ethereum ($ETH): -$93M• 📉 Solana ($SOL): -$25M pic.twitter.com/Muj58z2e4E

The reported data shows that Bitwise and other ETF clients sold approximately $25.08 million worth of SOL in the latest session. The extended absence of positive flows suggests that institutional demand has weakened during the ongoing correction.

ETF activity remains an important indicator of investor appetite, particularly as institutional products provide another route for traditional investors to gain exposure to Solana. A return to consistent inflows could help improve market confidence, while continued outflows may make a sustained recovery harder to establish.

Despite the continued decline, Solana’s technical indicators are showing a potentially encouraging development. Its price is making lower lows, while the RSI is moving higher, creating a bullish divergence.

$SOL is going down, but RSI is trending upThis is what happens when spot sellers are exhausted And every time, seller exhaustion brings a big pump pic.twitter.com/KkCRLxJdwf

This pattern suggests that selling momentum may be weakening even though the price remains under pressure. Such divergences can emerge near the later stages of a correction, when sellers begin losing strength and buyers gradually return.

However, RSI divergence does not guarantee an immediate reversal. SOL still needs stronger buying participation and a meaningful improvement in its price structure to confirm that the downtrend is losing control.

If the divergence develops into a broader recovery signal, it could create an opportunity for Solana to stabilise after its recent losses.

Solana’s near-term outlook remains cautious as weak ETF flows and a deteriorating price structure continue to weigh on the token. The lack of institutional demand also raises questions about how quickly buyers could return following the recent breakdown.

However, the improving RSI presents a potential counter-signal. If selling pressure continues to fade and spot demand recovers, SOL could attempt to reverse its recent losses.

The next phase will depend on whether this technical divergence attracts fresh buying interest or simply provides a temporary pause in the broader decline. For now, Solana’s recovery remains uncertain, but weakening selling momentum offers a reason to watch for a possible change in trend.

#5249. RLUSD Is Not Coming for XRP: Garlinghouse Clarifies Ripple’s Bigger XRPL Vision as Trader Spots Setup Behind 71% Price Explosion

Ripple CEO Bradley Garlinghouse is pushing back against the idea that the company’s growing RLUSD stablecoin ambitions come at XRP’s expense, insisting the stablecoin is targeting a different market altogether.

As Ripple sharpens its vision for the XRP Ledger, a separate development is drawing attention to XRP’s price prospects, with prominent crypto trader Ali Charts spotting a chart pattern that previously preceded a staggering 71% rally.

Garlinghouse sees the RLUSD stablecoin as a way to bring more activity and practical use cases to the XRP Ledger, not as a competitor to XRP. Instead of treating the stablecoin as a rival, he framed its growth as part of the broader momentum behind XRP, arguing that both assets can play complementary roles in expanding the ecosystem.

“RLUSD isn’t competing with XRP. It’s competing with other stablecoins. Use case matters, and I want those use cases running on the XRPL,” Garlinghouse wrote on X.

By targeting the wider market, Ripple hopes to expand the range of financial applications operating on its blockchain. Garlinghouse emphasized that the company wants RLUSD-powered use cases to run on XRPL, potentially attracting more businesses, developers, and institutional users to the network.

Garlinghouse was responding to XRP community researcher WrathofKahneman, who argued that RLUSD’s expansion could ultimately benefit XRP by increasing liquidity across the XRP Ledger. “RLUSD is great for XRP. More XRPL liquidity makes XRP easier to use in the long run & it isn’t replacing XRP where it wasn’t used,” the researcher wrote.

However, WrathofKahneman cautioned that the benefits may not immediately translate into significant price gains without direct demand for XRP. “The problem is that w/out direct use, price impact is 2nd order,” he added.

The researcher also raised a broader question about XRP’s future role in the ecosystem: “Will XRP become a specialized institutional asset with gated liquidity, or be ubiquitous?”

Agreed! RLUSD isn’t competing with XRP. It’s competing with other stablecoins. Use case matters, and I want those use cases running on the XRPL.

The debate is particularly relevant as XRP trades around $1.28, well below its previous all-time high of $3.65, even as Ripple continues to expand its institutional footprint. While growing adoption could strengthen the XRP Ledger, investors are still watching to see whether that progress will translate into stronger demand and sustained price appreciation for XRP.

Meanwhile, crypto analyst Ali Charts has identified a potentially bullish technical signal on XRP’s four-hour chart, suggesting the token could be gearing up for another significant move. According to the analyst, XRP recently recorded its tightest Bollinger Band squeeze since August before breaking above the upper band, which could signal building upward momentum.

The setup is drawing attention because a similar period of extreme volatility compression preceded an impressive rally earlier this year. Ali Charts noted that the last time XRP’s Bollinger Bands were this tightly compressed, the token surged nearly 71% in just three days.

The pundit believes another parabolic price move could now be taking shape. At its current price of around $1.16, a repeat of the previous 71% surge would push XRP to approximately $2.19. Such a move would represent a substantial recovery for the token, potentially bringing it closer to key resistance levels and reigniting bullish sentiment across the XRP market.

Traders will be watching whether XRP can sustain its move above the upper Bollinger Band and attract enough buying pressure to confirm a breakout. However, a failure to hold the gains could turn the latest bullish signal into another false start.

#5248. Bitcoin Price Falls Ahead of Jobs Report: Is a Fourth Sell-Off Inbound?

Bitcoin news: BTC closed below its 200-day EMA before the jobs report. It rose after 52 of 104 reports, but fell after the last 3.

In Bitcoin news on Friday, November 6, BTC heads into the US October jobs report at 8:30 a.m. ET after closing Thursday at $76,088. BTC USD price is now below its 200-day average for the first time since August 19.

The report itself has been a coin toss. The recent record has not.

Payroll employment rises by 165,000 in October; unemployment rate changes little at 4.1% https://t.co/ZwrVfLvQgj #JobsReport #BLSdata

— BLS-Labor Statistics (@BLS_gov) November 6, 2026

A Coinspeaker review of all 104 jobs reports since January 2018 shows Bitcoin was higher 24 hours later after exactly 52 of them. A week later, though, it was lower after each of the last three: down 3.3% in August, 5.2% in September and 3.7% in October.

The setup is already weak. Bitcoin trades at $76,160, down 5.1% in 24 hours, after Thursday’s chip-stock sell-off dragged it from $80,918 to $75,208, its lowest since September 16. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell from 50 to 28 in a day.

The jobs data also feeds straight into the Fed. Traders on Polymarket now price a 69% chance of a rate hike on December 9, down from 80% a day earlier.

So what does Bitcoin usually do after a jobs report, and can it win back the 200-day line?

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Not much to bet on the first day. The direction only starts to lean after a week, and only slightly.

We measured BTC from the hourly candle of each 8:30 a.m. ET release on Binance, using the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ release archive for the dates. The October 2025 report, never published because of the government shutdown, is not included.

This year broke into two halves. Bitcoin was higher a week after each of 2026’s first seven jobs reports, by 0.5% to 7.6%. Then it fell after all three since August.

One caveat: a week leaves room for other news to take over. The worst 24 hours in the sample came after the December 2021 report, a 17.1% drop that came with a weekend leverage flush.

DISCOVER: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

Because the Fed is leaning toward a hike, not a cut. It held rates at 3.75% to 4% on October 28 in a 10–2 vote, and both dissenters wanted a quarter-point hike.

Thursday’s crash already cooled that bet. Kalshi’s odds of a December hike dropped 10 points in a day, while a hold rose from 22% to 32%.

A strong report would likely push hike odds back up. A weak one would give the Fed room to wait, and with it, one less reason for traders to sell risk.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Not yet. BTC sits about $380 under its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $76,540, a line it had held on every daily close since its August breakout.

The jobs report has rarely set Bitcoin’s direction on the day. For traders following Bitcoin news this week, the weekly close against the 200-day EMA will matter more than the payroll number.

#5246. Binance Issues Crucial Update for Hyperliquid (HYPE) and Litecoin (LTC)

Binance has issued another important update on the batch re-opening of withdrawal services for tokens previously listed on Binance after the recent $6 billion attack forced the exchange to suspend the feature.

While Binance has remained consistent with the reopening of withdrawals for crypto assets in batches since the attack, Hyperliquid has drawn different attention as it remains the only top 10 cryptocurrency by market capitalization that has not been re-enabled since the attack.

Earlier today, Binance announced a deadline for the resumption of withdrawals for Hyperliquid (HYPE), Litecoin (LTC), and four other cryptocurrencies.

The announcement has come amid growing criticism from Hyperliquid holders who have remained affected by the delay in Hyperliquid's withdrawals on Binance.

Although Binance revealed that it is working to restore withdrawals for HYPE, LTC, Injective (INJ), Aptos (APT), Plasma (PLASMA), and NEAR Protocol (NEAR) by the end of next week, the criticism has grown even louder, with holders tagging Binance's co-founder Changpeng Zhao as unfair.

Despite Binance's appeal, the announcement has only triggered further backlash from the Hyperliquid community as they continue to question the reason behind the delay, since Binance has progressively restored withdrawals for dozens of other cryptocurrencies in the past week.

The growing criticism from the Hyperliquid community against Binance has given rise to several allegations against the exchange, with holders questioning the genuineness of the attack.

Notably, Hyperliquid holders have called on Binance to give clear explanations for excluding HYPE from earlier withdrawal restorations, arguing that there was no reason to keep the token locked since Hyperliquid was not affected by the attack.

Given Hyperliquid's growing adoption in the decentralized derivatives market, some critics have alleged that Binance is making intentional efforts to halt the asset's explosive growth.

XRP's 14-day Binance taker buy/sell ratio reached 0.998 on November 5, close to balance.

The ratio rose from 0.896 on November 2, while XRP fell from $1.25 to around $1.21.

Easing aggressive selling doesn't confirm a reversal; the possible impact of Binance's hack remains unverified.

XRP’s taker buy/sell ratio on Binance is moving toward balance, but the token’s price isn’t following suit. The 14-day simple moving average (SMA) reached 0.998 on November 5, when XRP traded at $1.206. That’s close to 1.0, suggesting aggressive buyers and sellers were trading at roughly equal volume.

It’s a notable shift. Just three days earlier, the ratio stood at 0.896. The seven-day average has also climbed to 0.976, pointing to easing selling pressure. Still, don’t mistake a move toward balance for a confirmed bullish reversal.

The price action tells a less encouraging story. XRP fell from $1.25 on November 2 to around $1.21 on November 5, even as the taker ratio improved.

In other words, aggressive selling on Binance appears to have eased, but buyers haven’t yet pushed the price higher. That distinction matters. A better ratio doesn’t automatically mean fresh demand has arrived.

Trading flows may also have been affected by the October 29 Binance hot-wallet hack, during which approximately $6.2 billion to $6.4 billion was stolen. Whether that event directly influenced XRP taker activity remains unverified.

The dollar index stood at 101.56, roughly unchanged over one month. However, this is a broader US-level measure, not a direct reading of XRP trading flows.

One possible explanation is that forced selling has cooled after recent declines. The Binance incident may also have influenced trading activity, but neither explanation is confirmed.

For now, the XRP taker buy/sell ratio offers a modest sign of easing pressure, not proof of a turnaround. The reading is based on a short window, and the claim that it reached its highest level since August still needs verification against the full historical series.

Stats from RWA.xyz shed more light on how XRP Ledger's leadership is constructed:

The key driver behind the tokenization breakthrough is JMWH fund by Justoken platform worth $2.23 billion. It represents tokenized contracts on electroenergy generation in Latin America, structured within Argentine and UK legal fields. At the moment there are 172 holders of this on-chain fund.

Meanwhile, BTC slipped from roughly $77,500 on October 31 to $75,800.

The underlying Exchange Whale Ratio nearly reached 1.0 on October 31. That meant large-holder transactions accounted for almost all measured exchange flow that day.

The 100-day average then rose from 0.481 on October 31 to 0.513 on November 6. This increase came as BTC struggled, falling 11.3% over one month despite remaining 17% higher over three months.

There’s an obvious complication. Binance suffered a hot-wallet hack on October 29, with approximately $6.2 billion to $6.4 billion reportedly stolen.

That incident may have affected large transfers during the same period. So, treating the rising whale ratio as straightforward evidence of deliberate selling would be premature. The available figures don’t establish what those large transactions represented.

US job openings reached 7.52 million in September, according to JOLTS data released November 3. The November 6 NFP report was also scheduled during this period.

The dollar index stood at 101.56, roughly unchanged over one month. These macro indicators provide background, but they don’t directly measure Binance whale activity. Any connection remains speculative.

One possible explanation is that transfers linked to the hack or reactions to macroeconomic data lifted the whale share. Neither explanation is verified.

For now, the Binance whale ratio shows rising large-holder activity alongside a weaker BTC price. But the series still needs verification, and the short observation window doesn’t establish whether whales are selling, repositioning or simply moving funds.

#5237. Gnosis Pay Breach Exposes User Data, Triggering Immediate Phishing Alerts

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Gnosis Pay, a fintech project from Britain, officially confirmed that data belonging to holders of its retail Visa debit cards was compromised. The breach which took place on November 3 continues the trend of this fall, when attackers no longer need to go after blockchains or smart contracts. It’s far easier for them to hit the traditional fiat infra that links digital assets to the real world.

Institutional partners and investors can exhale as the company’s enterprise and white-label B2B platform is running normally. For ordinary users, the key point is that the crypto in their wallets is safe, as the company said funds were not affected either. Card issuer Monavate Limited, which is regulated by the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority, continues to operate as well. The hackers walked away with data only.

This time the unauthorized access involved a legacy B2C card processing system. The Gnosis Pay platform was already being prepared for retirement, with a full shutdown scheduled for December 20. According to the official explanation, after the hack happened, Gnosis Pay’s security team moved fast to contain the threat and cut off access via the compromised keys within two hours.

The Gnosis Pay incident rounds out a trilogy of major leaks this fall and exposes a weak spot shared by crypto-fiat gateways. The timeline of the past few weeks points to a clear pattern evident in Ledger, Trezor, SafePal and Keystone leaks throughout 2026.

Gnosis Pay has finished emailing affected users with a detailed list of the exposed data. Until the system goes offline next month, the company is operating in emergency mode with transaction monitoring being upped, and 3D Secure verification is now mandatory for all online payments.

Of course, the company has also issued an urgent phishing alert. Armed with purchase details, addresses and personal data, scammers are already starting to pose as official customer support. The Gnosis Pay team urges users to be suspicious of all incoming requests and reminds them that “we and our Partner Apps will never ask” for security credentials such as seed phrases, private keys, PINs or full card numbers to verify or cancel transactions. Finally, any account changes are legitimate only when users make them directly within the official app.

#5236. Crypto’s Next Two Years Should Be About Survival, Not Competition: Vitalik Buterin

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has warned crypto executives to switch focus to collective security and survival rather than competition between platforms. This follows multiple hacks that drained billions from the market and crushed traders’ sentiment.

In an interview with MoneyControl, Buterin urged crypto executives to focus on protecting user assets as a collective, as that could shape how regulators approach the sector. The next couple of years are key, as frameworks are still expected in several jurisdictions.

Digital asset firms, particularly centralized exchanges, have focused on gaining a larger share of the market cap, onboarding more users, etc but this buzz around gains leaves room for bad actors. For Buterin, the actions in the next couple of years will determine the long-term roadmap.

Most crypto users agreed with the Ethereum executive because, without asset safety, centralized exchanges will see capital exodus and more backing from traditional finance firms.

Recently, several crypto companies were hacked, including Binance, the largest centralized exchange by trading volume. Bad actors flagged in North Korea drained $6 billion; although large parts were recovered, it still remains the largest crypto hack of all time.

This week, Brazil’s largest exchange, Mercado, also suffered a breach that temporarily suspended trading. In a nutshell, these losses could prompt regulators to tighten requirements, setting the sector back.

Previously, regulators in the US and Europe often cited investor-protection concerns to delay major developments that would open the sector to traditional capital. Notably, spot crypto ETFs are a top example, although things changed after the White House backed the move following President Trump’s election win.

Buterin also added that recent attacks now target user interfaces and centralized components rather than smart contracts. He called for more operations to move on-chain, citing Binance Smart Chain and others.

“One good decision that Binance made is that they also launched Binance Smart Chain. They also benefit from the fact that if you do things with contracts on-chain, you can have very high levels of security. I am expecting we’re going to see more moves in that direction.”

On Ethereum security, Buterin and developers rolled out a roadmap to protect assets ahead of Q-Day. The network is lauded for taking early steps ahead of others as supercomputers get more powerful.

#5233. Crypto exchanges tout cold storage ratios after Binance attack

Coinbase says it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline, while Gate reports 88.26% of its total assets are kept in cold storage.

Crypto exchanges were quick to reassure users following the attack on Binance’s hot wallet infrastructure last week, with several companies disclosing how they divide assets between cold storage and internet-connected hot wallets this week.

Crypto exchange Gate on Thursday launched a “Proof of Security” (PoSEC) framework, reporting that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage and 11.74% in hot wallets. It claims its cold storage could cover 104.58% of customer assets even if its hot wallets were completely drained.

“By publicly disclosing the distribution of assets between platform cold storage and hot wallets, PoSEC provides visibility into asset storage structures and their ability to cover potential losses under extreme scenarios,” Gate said. It noted the data is still undergoing independent review by a third-party audit firm.

Threat actors attacked Binance’s hot-wallet infrastructure last week, stealing approximately $6.36 billion, most of it in about 20 minutes, according to TRM Labs. Binance CEO Richard Teng said the “vast majority” of user assets are held in cold wallets, but the company has not provided a precise split.

Other crypto exchanges have been quick to share their cold storage ratios this week.

In a blog post Wednesday, Coinbase said that more than 99% of customer assets are held in offline cold storage and that it continuously rebalances excess assets to cold storage.

“Binance’s reported hot wallet incident has understandably left customers asking how Coinbase protects customer assets from something similar happening here,” it said.

On Tuesday, Upbit, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in South Korea, confirmed it holds 99.17% of its assets in cold wallets, with the remaining 0.83% in hot wallets as of September 2026. These figures are already disclosed to the Financial Supervisory Service.

“This represents the highest cold wallet storage ratio among South Korea’s five major KRW-based cryptocurrency exchanges and is substantially above the regulatory minimum of 80%,” a spokesperson for Upbit parent company Dunamu told Cointelegraph, in response to questions about South Korea’s call for crypto exchanges to increase their cold storage ratios.

“Our aim is to keep our hot wallet holdings at an absolute minimum, with a target of maintaining them below 1% of customer digital assets,” they added.

Related: Fed, OCC check US banks after Binance hack as experts flag security risks

Other major South Korean exchanges have reported lower cold-wallet shares. Financial Supervisory Service figures cited in earlier reporting put Bithumb at 94.76%, Coinone at 85%, Digital X, formerly Korbit, at 82.79%, and GOPAX at 80.54% at the end of September.

OKX’s existing security overview, last updated on Sept. 18, 2026, said it holds more than 95% of client crypto assets in cold wallets and less than 5% in hot wallets.

The reported ratios are not necessarily directly comparable because exchanges use different reporting periods and may calculate cold-storage shares against different asset bases.

Cold storage ratios, however, offer only part of the picture of an exchange’s security.

Offline wallets can still be exposed through compromised signing systems, inadequate access controls or employees approving fraudulent transactions.

Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission warned in an August 2025 circular that such weaknesses could compromise both hot- and cold-wallet infrastructure.

#5227. Chainalysis says breach exposed password hashes and live tokens

Chainalysis disclosed password hashes and live tokens were exposed after initially reporting only non-sensitive customer data was accessed.

Chainalysis on Wednesday disclosed a wider impact from a cyberattack it initially described as involving only non-sensitive customer information.

“On Monday, we discovered certain customer information including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed to a malicious actor,” the blockchain analytics firm said in an update to its incident notice.

The company did not disclose whether each type of information was exposed for every user and declined to provide Cointelegraph with additional information beyond its published disclosure.

Chainalysis initially said on Oct. 30 that the intrusion exposed user IDs, names and email addresses but found no evidence that attackers accessed authentication credentials or session tokens.

Another Wednesday update stated an “on-path attack” exposed some customers’ passwords. The company said it had contained and remediated that attack vector and was locking affected accounts and requiring password resets.

Despite the broader exposure, Chainalysis said it still had no evidence that attackers accessed investigation data or manipulated its attribution data.

#5224. Chainalysis Begins Restoring Screening Services After Disclosing Exposed Password Hashes

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Chainalysis said on November 6 it was restoring KYT and address screening in phases after a cyberattack. The firm earlier disclosed that names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for users had been exposed. Customers were told to prepare password resets and API-key rotation; investigations data exposure has not been established.

A disruption at one of cryptocurrency’s best-known investigative and compliance providers is also a test of operational resilience for the companies that depend on it. In a security incident notice updated November 6, Chainalysis said it had begun restoring access to its Know Your Transaction, or KYT, and address-screening products through a phased process.

The restoration followed several days of service restrictions and increasingly detailed disclosures about a cyberattack. Because many crypto businesses use screening tools to investigate suspicious transactions or meet compliance obligations, this is a story about both information security and the ability of regulated operations to continue.

Chainalysis initially reported discovering unauthorised activity affecting its internal systems and tools. Its October 30 statement said it had found no evidence at that point of access to certain sensitive materials. But the November 4 update disclosed that user information, including names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens, had been exposed to an attacker.

That sequence is important. Early incident statements often reflect a limited investigation, and later forensic work can establish a wider impact. The responsible reading is the latest dated disclosure, not a permanently frozen version of the first announcement.

The company also reported abnormal activity around KYT and other screening tools, prompting additional products to be taken offline. Chainalysis said it had no evidence of access to investigation content or manipulation of its attribution data at the time of its updates. That is a narrower claim than declaring every possible effect ruled out.

Chainalysis told customers to submit trusted IP addresses for allowlisting and prepare to reset passwords and rotate API keys as access is restored. A password hash is not the same as a plaintext password, but exposed hashes create security concerns depending on how they were generated and the strength of the underlying credentials. Live tokens can present a separate risk because they may enable access while valid.

For organisations, the operational response should follow the vendor’s direct instructions and their own security teams’ assessment. Users should not click unexpected reset links in unsolicited emails; signing in through a verified service address is safer than relying on a message that could be spoofed.

The wider issue of controls and dependency is also present in NewsBTC’s coverage of Aave’s protective restrictions on new tBTC positions. Different systems and risks are involved, but both illustrate how a provider’s status can affect the options available to dependent services.

Compliance teams need accurate screening, audit trails and clear decisions about when they can accept funds or process an onboarding request. Temporarily losing a primary tool can complicate those processes even if the underlying blockchain continues operating. Backups, manual escalation and incident playbooks are therefore part of real crypto infrastructure.

Chainalysis said restoration would expand as it validated enhanced security controls. It had not, in the cited November 6 update, confirmed full restoration of every affected product. That distinction should guide reporting and customer decisions.

The key future questions are the complete scope of exposure, remedial actions, the timetable for Reactor and other affected products and independent assurance that compromised credentials have been invalidated. For now, the firm has acknowledged a serious security incident and begun a controlled recovery.

#5222. ChatGPT Is Getting a GIF Maker Powered by OpenAI's Unannounced Images 2.6 Model

ChatGPT Is Getting a GIF Maker Powered by OpenAI's Unannounced Images 2.6 Model

The internet may soon have an unlimited supply of AI-generated dancing cats, courtesy of ChatGPT.

OpenAI is rolling out a feature that lets users generate animated GIFs directly inside ChatGPT, according to The Verge. The feature reportedly comes powered by its new image-generation model called Images 2.6, which OpenAI has yet to formally introduce through its usual product announcements.

Users can describe an animation in plain English or upload an existing photo and ask ChatGPT to bring it to life. Once the GIF is generated, they can adjust its playback speed, inspect individual frames, make edits, and share the finished animation.

OpenAI demonstrated the capability with a simple request: “can you make a gif of a cat dancing?” The resulting interface reportedly includes controls to change animation speed and examine the GIF frame by frame.

We tried generating GIFs using ChatGPT, but the feature was not available on our accounts at the time of testing. In our interaction, the model generates a series of frames, but not the animation.

The rollout appears to be gradual, so users may have to keep asking for their dancing cats a little longer.

The GIF maker is reportedly part of a broader Images 2.6 update that promises faster image generation. The Verge reports that OpenAI is bringing the model to ChatGPT and Codex users across web, desktop, and mobile platforms.

Developers are also getting two new API models, GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst, designed for faster generation and higher-quality results, respectively. OpenAI has not yet published a standalone announcement detailing the new model's capabilities, and we could not independently test its performance.

The update follows the September release of ChatGPT Images 2.5, which introduced sharper details, more precise editing, and generation speeds up to 50% faster than its predecessor.

In our previous testing, Images 2.5 went head-to-head with Google's Nano Banana 2 across six categories, with each model winning three. OpenAI's model delivered particularly impressive illustration quality and improved on the oversharpening problems that affected earlier versions, although it still made mistakes when rendering text.

The move into GIF generation also comes months after OpenAI shut down Sora, its standalone AI video-generation app, in March. Animated GIFs are considerably simpler than the videos Sora generated, but the new feature brings a form of motion generation directly into ChatGPT without requiring a separate application.

OpenAI has not provided a specific date for when every ChatGPT account will receive GIF generation.

#5220. Nasdaq Lists Canary’s Staked INJ ETF, Adding Another Route to Altcoin Exposure

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Nasdaq began listing the Canary Staked INJ ETF under ticker INJC on November 5, according to the exchange’s listing notice and Canary Capital. The product seeks Injective token exposure and staking rewards, but fund ownership is not the same as directly holding or controlling INJ.

US exchange-traded cryptocurrency products are extending well beyond Bitcoin and Ether. Nasdaq’s November 4 trader notice confirmed that the Canary Staked INJ ETF would be listed starting Thursday, November 5, under the ticker INJC. Canary Capital’s launch announcement describes the fund’s aim as exposure to INJ, the native token of the Injective network, together with an ability to earn staking rewards.

That gives investors a new route into a smaller cryptocurrency using a familiar brokerage account. It also adds a layer of product structure and fees that should not be confused with direct ownership of tokens in a self-custodied wallet.

Injective operates a proof-of-stake blockchain. In proof-of-stake networks, eligible token holders can participate in network validation, often by delegating tokens to validators, and may receive rewards. A staked fund seeks to reflect some of that economics through its holdings and operations.

Canary says net staking rewards will be reflected in the ETF’s net asset value. The word ‘net’ matters: fund expenses, staking arrangements, validator performance and timing can affect the value delivered to shareholders. Investors should examine the prospectus for the risks, fee structure and precise mechanics rather than treating a possible reward as a fixed interest payment.

Nasdaq’s notice identifies the designated liquidity provider and the start of trading and valuation dissemination. That is concrete evidence of a listed product. It does not by itself establish investor demand, daily liquidity under every market condition or what the shares will trade at relative to their underlying net asset value.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs have become widely followed because their fund creations and redemptions provide a visible gauge of flows through conventional investment channels. NewsBTC’s recent analysis of Bitcoin ETF outflows illustrates why even those large products can see very different activity from day to day.

A smaller-token fund adds different considerations. The underlying market may be thinner, its network risks more specialised and its investor base less developed than that of Bitcoin. Product suitability depends on the actual structure and an investor’s ability to withstand volatility, not simply on the convenience of buying a ticker.

There is also a difference between a fund seeking staking economics and an account that allows an investor to select their own validator, manage keys or participate directly in onchain governance. The listed wrapper handles custody and operational choices through fund service providers.

The useful follow-up figures are shares outstanding, assets under management, realised flows, bid-ask spreads, trading volumes, fees and how staking income is accounted for. These will tell readers more than a single day’s INJ price move or the excitement surrounding a new listing.

The wider lesson is that the ETF market is developing more specialised structures. That can expand financial access while moving key operational decisions away from end users. INJC’s listing is a verified milestone. Whether it becomes a durable and liquid product remains to be demonstrated by its trading record.

#5215. Amundi Puts a European Equity Fund Share Class on Ethereum

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Amundi has launched a tokenised share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on public Ethereum, working with CACEIS. It is a real fund share-class initiative, not a claim that all 600 constituent stocks are individually trading as permissionless tokens around the clock.

One of Europe’s biggest asset managers has moved a conventional index product into the world of tokenised fund units. In a November 2026 announcement, Amundi said a new share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 strategy had been issued on public Ethereum, using infrastructure developed with CACEIS.

That matters because asset tokenisation is often discussed in abstract terms. Here, the starting point is an existing diversified European equity strategy and a new way of recording or distributing interests in it.

Amundi’s Core STOXX Europe 600 tracks a broad European equity benchmark. What the firm has announced is a tokenised share class of the fund. It has not said that every underlying company has issued new public blockchain shares or that investors can automatically trade each of those stocks at any hour.

The distinction is fundamental. In a fund structure, an investor owns units governed by the fund’s legal terms. The fund, in turn, holds or tracks the underlying basket according to its mandate. Tokenising the unit can change the infrastructure used for issuance, transfer or recordkeeping without changing the basic economic exposure of the underlying investment strategy.

The company says the traditional distribution model remains available. The Ethereum-linked share class is integrated into the existing operating model rather than replacing the fund’s conventional administration overnight.

Amundi highlights potential benefits including operational efficiency, quicker settlement, transparency and improved distribution. These are plausible advantages of shared digital records, but each depends on regulatory acceptance, custodianship, identity controls and the systems connecting a blockchain to conventional fund administration.

CACEIS’s role is important because a token cannot, by itself, maintain every legal and administrative function expected of a regulated fund. Shareholder rights, transfer restrictions, reconciliation, accounting and redemption procedures still require well-defined responsible parties.

The effort follows earlier Amundi work involving tokenised money-market products and subscriptions using stablecoins. That progression suggests the asset manager is testing multiple financial use cases rather than assuming one technology will immediately replace existing market infrastructure.

NewsBTC recently examined the NYSE’s planned tokenised securities venue and its transfer-agent partners. The US exchange’s programme and Amundi’s European fund are distinct, but both underline the importance of ownership records and operational plumbing. A blockchain timestamp alone does not resolve an investor-rights question.

The most useful measurements will be actual eligible investors using the new share class, the cost and speed of subscriptions and redemptions, secondary-transfer rules and how issuers handle corporate actions and compliance. Amundi has not published enough in the cited announcement to quantify all these outcomes.

There is also no reason to equate demand for tokenised fund units with a guaranteed effect on ETH’s market price. Transaction fees and onchain activity are one component of a much larger network economy, and adoption can grow without a direct one-for-one connection to token valuations.

The development is meaningful because it involves an established asset manager applying public blockchain infrastructure to an actual investment product. The next chapter is operational evidence: whether the new representation makes fund ownership simpler, cheaper or more accessible without compromising the protections investors expect.

#5214. Why Bitcoin's Next Soft Fork Could Feel Like a Practice Run

Why Bitcoin's Next Soft Fork Could Feel Like a Practice Run

Four flaws in Bitcoin’s consensus rules that have lingered for years.

Issues like quantum resistance may command attention, but a practical cleanup is what many experts think Bitcoin’s next soft fork is likely to address, spanning fixes for vulnerabilities in the network’s difficulty adjustment mechanism to denial-of-service vectors among miners.

Proposed in 2019 and known as the Great Consensus Cleanup (BIP-54), the upgrade seeks to address the “cruft” in Bitcoin’s consensus design through changes that have historically been sidelined, as described by long-time Bitcoin developer and BIP-54 co-author Matt Corallo.

“There’s a laundry list of things we know of that we really need to clean up,” he said during a recent appearance on MARA Foundation TV. “All of these issues are real concerns that could impact Bitcoin negatively, but they’re not like, ‘Oh, the sky is falling.’”

Although a formal timeline for the BIP’s undertaking hasn’t been established, Corallo thinks there’s an 80% chance that the Great Consensus Cleanup is up next for the network. During his talk with Head of MARA Foundation Isabel Foxen Duke, he also called it a practical exercise for Bitcoin developers who haven’t yet been through a soft fork.

At its core, Corallo said BIP-54 “fixes some stuff that everyone agrees are problems,” while targeting four specific vulnerabilities:

Still, not everyone views a maintenance-focused soft fork as a major win. On X, Paul Sztorc, co-founder and CEO of LayerTwo Labs, called BIP-54’s potential activation “kind of depressing, since it is a janitorial maintenance fork that doesn't do anything.”

Surveying developers at TABconf in Atlanta, Sztorc noted that Bitcoin’s “best and brightest” predominantly expect the Great Consensus Cleanup to be Bitcoin’s next soft fork anyway, with the earliest estimate in September 2027, and most pointing to 2028 or later.

Following the activation of Taproot in 2021, Bitcoin’s community has faced years of gridlock surrounding protocol changes. This friction is frequently framed around “ossification,” with broader protocol changes like OP_CAT (BIP-347) and OP_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY (BIP-119) struggling to reach ecosystem-wide consensus.

According to Corallo, soft forks have always involved overcoming technical hurdles. But more recently, he’s observed political and social friction that’s become just as relevant.

The Bitcoin community spent months debating how Taproot should be activated, with arguments pitting miner-signaling thresholds against mandatory user flag days. Corallo argues that BIP-54 can establish a deployment playbook for future soft forks.

“In every recent soft fork, there’s also been a bunch of drama about activation mechanisms,” he said. “So hopefully we could do a soft fork to go through that drama, and then copy and paste and reuse it and head off some of that drama [for future soft forks].”

In that sense, BIP-54 is just as much about proving Bitcoin can still agree on upgrades at the social layer as it is about actual code cleanup.

#5211. Coinbase Pitches a Full Token Lifecycle Service, From Public Sales to Custody

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Coinbase’s November 5 product update describes an integrated set of services for token issuers, from sales and distribution through listings, custody and liquidity. It cites Monad, Ethena and Hyperliquid as examples, but the examples are company-selected and do not eliminate the risks or regulatory limits facing token projects.

For a blockchain project, issuing a token may be the relatively easy part. Finding real users, managing custody, listing on exchanges and supporting institutional trading each introduce complicated operational decisions. In a November 5 announcement, Coinbase presented those tasks as parts of one integrated platform for token issuers.

The pitch is straightforward: use fewer separate service providers and reduce the number of operational handoffs. For developers and investors, the interesting question is how much of that convenience comes from genuine technical integration and how much reflects the commercial advantage of a large incumbent bundling its own services.

Coinbase pointed to a public MON token sale involving an affiliate of Monad Foundation, describing more than 85,000 purchasers in over 70 countries. It said the token now has more than 150,000 unique traders and $7.2 billion in spot volume on its platform. Those are company-reported measures from a chosen example, not a representative result for every issuer that uses similar services.

With Ethena, Coinbase described a relationship that expanded from token-management tools into institutional custody, wallets and trading. It also cited a USDC-related product and hundreds of millions of dollars in new deposits. For Hyperliquid, the company emphasised its role in deploying USDC treasury infrastructure and supporting large transfers.

The three examples involve different business models, market structures and needs. They demonstrate possible uses for the platform, but readers should not assume that success in one project translates directly into another token’s demand or risk profile.

Bundling services can remove duplicate work for a project team. One integration may simplify onboarding, compliance coordination and support. It can also make changing suppliers harder if critical functions become dependent on the same provider.

A token issuer should examine who legally controls assets at every stage, what happens if a service is paused, how withdrawal requests are handled and whether exchanges and custodians have the right safeguards for each market. Convenience is not a substitute for operational resilience.

That issue connects to NewsBTC’s earlier coverage of Coinbase’s restrictions on certain stablecoins for EEA customers. An exchange service can be available in one region but restricted in another without changing the underlying token network. Eligibility and local regulation remain part of any credible launch plan.

Coinbase also said it is broadening work around tokenised equities and access to private markets. Those plans should be distinguished from products already live and from securities that may require additional identity or jurisdictional checks.

The practical questions go beyond transaction volume: what are the total fees, the terms of custody, the geographic eligibility limits, support commitments and data-portability arrangements? What functions can an issuer replace if its needs change? Where do responsibilities sit when an incident affects users across several services?

NewsBTC recently examined the operational requirements of tokenised securities venues, where ownership records and corporate actions remain essential despite the appeal of blockchain settlement.

Coinbase’s new presentation shows how major crypto platforms are positioning themselves as end-to-end service providers rather than standalone exchanges. Whether that gives issuers better outcomes will depend on transparency, competition and the performance of the services after the marketing presentation ends.

#5210. Why aren’t XLM crypto traders betting big before the 23 November vote?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Stellar’s [XLM] next upgrade just cleared its testnet vote. Validators will decide on the mainnet version in a couple of weeks.

Hence, the question – Has the token’s price moved in lockstep?

Bell (also known as Protocol 30), cleared its testnet vote on 3rd November. Validators will vote on the mainnet version on the 23rd.

According to the Stellar Development Foundation, Bell would bring three changes. The first will involve letting smart contract tell payments for different customers apart. This would make life immensely easier for businesses.

The second change will allow smart contracts check post-quantum signatures as the network’s own signatures would stay the same. The last would switch ledger timing to milliseconds. Here, it’s worth noting that they’ve admitted that this change along won’t make blocks faster.

Also, 23rd is not the final launch date. In fact, Bell only goes live if validators approve it, with the Foundation clarifying that the date could still move.

In the meantime, wallets, exchanges and node operators need to update their software.

Ideally, an upgrade would put the price up on its shoulders. Not this one though.

XLM went up to about $0.171 on the 4th, then came tumbling down the next afternoon. It’s been stuck between $0.153 and $0.157 since. At press time, it was valued at around $0.155.

Indicators seemed to be indecisive. The RSI was at 45.2, under the Signal Line. The ADX on the DMI was at around 18.5. What did this indicate? Well, there didn’t seem to be a strong trend either way, though sellers were just slightly ahead.

Futures traders have mostly taken a few steps back too. Open interest dropped from about $94 million to $88 million during the slide and at the time of writing, it was $89.5 million. Funding was barely positive at 0.0011% too.

Simply put, it may be evident that everyone’s playing it safe. No one’s betting big before the big 23rd November vote. For now, $0.16 is the level to watch.

#5208. Elliptic Traces $124M in Bitcoin Swaps From Binance Hack Funds

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: A November 6 update from blockchain intelligence firm Elliptic says roughly $124 million of assets stolen in the October Binance breach had been converted into Bitcoin, including funds originally held as XRP and SOL. Onchain tracing can reveal movement, but it cannot by itself identify every person controlling those wallets or prove that all the converted funds have been cashed out.

The laundering trail from the huge October cryptocurrency theft attributed by investigators to North Korean-linked actors continues to evolve. In a November 6 update to its technical analysis, Elliptic said the value of stolen assets converted into Bitcoin had reached approximately $124 million.

The headline figure is striking, but the more useful story concerns how the funds moved, what remains traceable and why conversion into Bitcoin is not the same as spending money through the conventional financial system.

Elliptic’s investigation describes activity involving tens of thousands of wallets, multiple networks and an assortment of services. By its November 6 checkpoint, analysts had identified about 1,650 BTC held in new addresses following conversion from other stolen assets. The firm said roughly $50 million worth of XRP had begun moving largely towards Bitcoin, while stolen Solana tokens had also been swapped, bridged or mixed.

The firm presented this as an ongoing, rapidly changing investigation. An estimated figure tied to a timestamp should not be reported as a permanent total, and wallet clusters can change as further transactions occur.

Cross-chain movement complicates tracing because the deposit and payout sides of a transfer may occur on different networks. It can also make the trail harder to follow when funds pass through pools, aggregators and intermediaries. However, the public nature of blockchain transactions and the ability to connect wallet activity through known services can still help investigators reconstruct substantial portions of the flow.

Elliptic reported that approximately $2.85 billion of the original stolen assets had been frozen and about $3.11 billion remained in addresses linked to the theft at its latest checkpoint. The firm cautioned that only a negligible portion appeared to have been cashed out. Such estimates may change with later tracing, and asset values vary with market prices.

This matters because a criminal actor may hold large amounts of Bitcoin or Ether for some time before attempting to move value through brokers or exchanges. Public addresses can show coins being shuffled, but they generally cannot prove the real-world identity of each subsequent controller or the final ownership arrangement.

The distinction is especially relevant to compliance services. Screening against attributed addresses can alert businesses to potential sanctions or illicit-funds exposure, even when the funds have crossed networks. Yet address blacklists and automated risk scoring are not perfect substitutes for investigation and human judgement.

The evolving theft occurred alongside a different security incident affecting Chainalysis, another blockchain-analysis provider. The two incidents should not be conflated. Chainalysis described its own systems and credentials issue as unrelated to the Binance theft, while Elliptic’s work here concerns tracing funds from that separate exchange incident.

For operators, the lesson connects to the custody, counterparty and incident-response themes covered in NewsBTC’s reporting on digital-asset infrastructure restrictions. Protecting users involves controls over withdrawals, counterparties and incident communications — not simply watching one chain’s transaction explorer.

The next meaningful updates will concern verified freezes, attributed movements to identifiable services and evidence of actual cash-out. Elliptic’s data show the stolen funds are still moving through complex paths. They do not yet tell a complete story about who ultimately receives them or how much can be recovered.

#5207. Arkansas Sues Kalshi, Joining a Growing List of States Targeting Prediction Markets

Arkansas Sues Kalshi, Joining a Growing List of States Targeting Prediction Markets

Arkansas has sued Kalshi, accusing the prediction market of offering an illegal, unregulated gambling platform to the state's residents, Attorney General Tim Griffin said on Wednesday.

The lawsuit, filed against KalshiEX LLC and Kalshi Inc., alleges multiple violations of the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act. The state is seeking restitution, penalties, taxes and an injunction.

Today I filed a lawsuit against @Kalshi for violating the Arkansas Deceptive Trade Practices Act by operating an unregulated gambling platform.

Kalshi has built a global business that it calls a prediction market, allowing consumers to wager money on the outcome of just about… pic.twitter.com/ePycNKXzy6

— Attorney General Tim Griffin (@AGTimGriffin) November 4, 2026

"It doesn't take a genius to understand that wagering money on whether the Razorbacks win or lose is gambling," Griffin said. "And gambling on an unregulated platform is squarely prohibited by Arkansas law."

Instead of obtaining licenses and paying the taxes required of gambling operators, Kalshi opened its platform to Arkansas residents as young as 18 and encouraged them to bet on sporting and entertainment events, Griffin alleged. "Arkansas law is concerned with substance, not semantics," he said.

Griffin pointed to Kalshi's own responsible-gambling tools, including self-exclusion, deposit limits and trading breaks, along with its partnership with the National Council on Problem Gambling, as evidence that the company knows its platform carries gambling-style risks. "Although Kalshi insists that its products are not gambling, its actions speak louder than its labels," he said.

Kalshi, which is regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, has argued in other cases that its event contracts fall under exclusive federal jurisdiction and are not subject to state gambling laws.

Arkansas is the latest of more than a dozen states to take on prediction markets. Among the most significant cases:

Other states have also moved against prediction markets. Arizona filed criminal charges against Kalshi in March, a Washington court temporarily blocked its sports contracts in July, and Massachusetts' case is now before the state's highest court after a lower court barred Kalshi's sports contracts in January.

The CFTC has sued at least 10 states to defend what it says is its exclusive authority over prediction markets, and President Donald Trump has backed the agency, calling several state officials who challenged the platforms "scum."

Federal appeals courts are split. The Third Circuit ruled in April that New Jersey cannot regulate Kalshi's sports contracts, while the Sixth and Ninth Circuits sided with Ohio, Tennessee and Nevada. New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to settle the question, backed by 39 other states and the District of Columbia, as well as the NFL. Kalshi's response to the petition is due November 9, and the Supreme Court is not expected to decide whether to take up the case until December at the earliest, ESPN reported.

The HYPE treasury company spent $785 million on tokens during the quarter and wants to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.

A subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed HYPE treasury company Hyperliquid Strategies has applied to become a futures commission merchant (FCM), seeking to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.

“Owning HYPE is how we aim to capture economics associated with the Hyperliquid protocol; setting up an FCM is how we intend to help bring markets deployed on Hyperliquid onshore,” said Hyperliquid Strategies CEO David Schamis in the company’s results for the quarter ended Sept. 30, published on Thursday.

Hyperliquid’s HIP-3 framework allows independent operators to launch custom perpetual futures markets on the protocol’s onchain infrastructure by staking 500,000 HYPE tokens ($38.8 million). Proposed HIP-3 features would allow operators to create permissioned markets that restrict participation to approved addresses.

The subsidiary would handle US customer accounts for permissioned markets deployed on Hyperliquid, the company said. Both the FCM application and the proposed markets require regulatory approval.

Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, announced an agreement with Trade[XYZ] on Oct. 29 to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual markets to the US, subject to regulatory approvals. ICE plans to operate a dedicated market and clearing structure.

#5205. Bitcoin ETFs could surpass mutual funds in AUM by 2028: Bloomberg analyst

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

As we are about to enter the third year of the Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETF being launched, it appears that BTC ETFs have a significantly stronger influence on BTC price returns than corporate Bitcoin accumulation.

According to the latest analysis by Ecoinometrics, an inflow of 10,000 BTC into spot Bitcoin ETFs corresponds to an estimated 3.2% boost in monthly Bitcoin returns. In comparison, the same amount of Bitcoin purchased by public companies contributes approximately 0.7% to monthly returns.

This suggests that ETF purchases have roughly 4.5 times the impact of corporate buying on Bitcoin’s price performance.

Adding more to this analysis, Bloomberg’s James Seyffart suggests that ETFs could surpass mutual funds in total Assets Under Management (AUM) within the next two to three years.

Their growth is only accelerating. If we stay on the same trend we’ve been on since the summer it will happen in ~two years.

Confirming his prediction, Syeffart used a chart and highlighted that ETFs accounted for 40.21% of total fund assets as of September 2026. And given the recent growth trends, ETFs could reach the 50% mark as early as September 2028 if the three-month growth rate continues.

However, other projections estimate this milestone between November 2028 and December 2029, depending on the period considered.

At the same time, ETFs rolling 12-month growth rate have also reached 3.74% in September 2026, above the historical average of 2.78% since the 2020 COVID market bottom. This indicates that ETF adoption is expanding faster than its long-term average.

This comes as BTC ETFs are in their outflows streak. According to Farisde Investors data, from 1st to 5th November 2026, Bitcoin ETFs saw mostly outflows. In fact, so far in November, it has already recorded $869.82 million in outflows. The only exception being on the 4th of November, when the BTC ETFs recorded a net inflow of $74.6 million.

All of this happened as the price of BTC was trading at $76,102.46 after a drop of 52% in the past 24 hours.

That said, besides Bitcoin ETFs, Ethereum [ETH] ETFs also recorded $272.09  in outflows, and Binance [BNB] ETFs recorded $271.01K in outflows. Meanwhile, XRP ETFs were funded by $529.51K in outflows, Solana [SOL] ETFs had $1.18M in outflows, and Hyperliquid [HYPE] ETFs also saw $7.66 million in outflows.

In short, the pattern suggests risk-off sentiment across crypto at the start of November, and not just in Bitcoin. So, given the current data, it remains to be seen whether Seyffart’s predictions turn into reality or not.

#5204. Aave Buys Avon Team to Bring More Fixed-Rate Lending Onchain

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Aave Labs said November 6 it had acquired Avon’s team and technology, including fixed- and floating-rate lending systems and an onchain order book. The move adds expertise for fixed-rate borrowing, but does not mean a finished fixed-rate Aave product has launched for every user.

Most people who take out a conventional loan want a clear answer to one question: what interest rate will they pay over the borrowing period? Decentralised finance often works differently, with interest rates that vary as supply and demand change within a lending pool. Aave Labs wants to broaden that model and has taken a new step towards it.

In its November 6 acquisition announcement, the company said it had bought the team and technology behind Avon, a developer focused on fixed-rate and floating-rate lending markets. The transaction includes Avon’s onchain order book, protocols, domains and other related assets. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The Aave release says Avon engineers Prince Sinha and Ayush Kaul will join the engineering team, while Omar el-Ashaal will join business development. Their stated focus includes fixed-rate lending and new types of onchain credit products.

A fixed rate can help borrowers plan expenses and hedge uncertainty. But supplying a dependable fixed-rate loan onchain requires more than setting a number at origination. Liquidity must be available over the loan’s term, interest-rate risk has to be allocated, collateral can change in value and lenders must be compensated for taking duration and credit-related risks.

Avon’s order-book technology could be relevant because an order book offers a different way to match borrowing and lending preferences compared with a purely pool-based floating-rate market. The acquisition does not itself prove that a design has completed security audits, won any required governance approval or become accessible to ordinary customers.

Aave describes itself as the largest onchain lending network, reporting more than $33 billion of deposits and $13 billion of active loans in its announcement. Those figures are company-reported and can fluctuate with token prices, collateral flows and market conditions.

The project already supports variable-rate borrowing and multiple asset markets. NewsBTC recently covered Aave’s protective freeze on new tBTC borrowing and supply, a reminder that risk settings and asset-specific decisions remain important even on an automated lending platform.

Fixed-rate capability could be useful to fintech partners and institutions that want more predictable liability management. It could also introduce complexities around maturity dates, rates, early repayment and liquidation that need careful contract design.

Aave Labs builds products that interact with the broader Aave network, but governance and the status of each deployed market matter. The acquisition is a corporate development and an engineering investment, not a guarantee that a new borrowing market is live today or approved across jurisdictions.

In NewsBTC’s prior reporting on Aave’s first externally curated V4 markets, the responsibility for risk settings and the structure of individual lending markets emerged as central questions. Fixed-rate lending will face similar scrutiny.

What should users watch for next? Published product specifications, audited contracts, governance decisions, clear rate and repayment terms, and evidence of sustainable liquidity. Aave’s acquisition explains the direction of travel: bringing more familiar credit-market features onchain. Whether users get the predictability they expect will depend on how those features are actually designed and deployed.

Ripple contributed to a white paper commissioned by the Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA), which brings together perspectives and  insights from leading practitioners across the financial services ecosystem.

Ripple's Managing Director, Middle East & Africa, Reece Merrick, recently stated his contribution to  the DFSA's new publication: "Scaling Tokenization: The Road Ahead," alongside leaders from BlackRock, Standard Chartered and Robinhood.

The white paper considers the conditions that may support the responsible scaling of tokenised financial assets and related market infrastructure, including within the Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC).

Aside from Merrick, other contributors include Tony Ashraf, Managing Director, Head of Technology & Operations and Head of Digital Assets, Middle East & Africa at BlackRock; Coy Garrison, Senior Director and Deputy General Counsel, Crypto at Robinhood; René Michau, Global Head, Digital Asset Advisory at Standard Chartered;  Henson Orser, Founder and Chief  Executive at Soter Insure; and Herman Schueller, Director, Innovation and Technology Risk Supervision at DFSA.

According to the DFSA report, tokenization of traditional financial assets has the potential to become a significant development in mainstream financial markets, offering the prospect of greater access for investors, increased efficiency for issuers and intermediaries, and reduced risk in certain areas, especially around settlement, for the wider financial system.

Merrick shared his perspective, saying that the real shift is not just tokenized treasuries and MMFs (Money Market Funds) gaining AUM but rather their on-chain utility as collateral in repo and margin without needing to redeem to cash first. This viewpoint follows as repo markets continue to move trillions daily, with Merrick highlighting this as potential for tokenization.

Merrick anticipates massive growth in this regard over the next 12 months, predicting that a significant proportion of that will be on the XRP Ledger.

"With clear frameworks, institutional custody, and trusted settlement assets like RLUSD, the UAE, DIFC and Ripple are positioned at the forefront of this next phase," Merrick stated.

Forecasts for the future size of tokenised assets vary considerably. Citi Institute's base case is for the global market in tokenised financial assets to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030.  A Standard Chartered and Synpulse paper estimated that demand for tokenised assets could reach $30.1 trillion by 2034.

Dogecoin community member Mishaboar has raised concerns about the security risks associated with social signing, a feature that allows users to create and access a blockchain wallet using everyday accounts like Google, Apple ID, Telegram, or email instead of managing a complex seed phrase.

This comes after Keplr, a multichain wallet supporting Cosmos, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Starknet, stated it had received reports of unauthorized transactions on some Keplr accounts created with Google or Apple login.

The wallet provider stated that the incident has been escalated to the Web3Auth team, with both working together to investigate the matter.

Before Keplr's disclosure, Web3 wallet infrastructure provider Web3Auth said it was aware of a security issue affecting Web3Auth's services used by some third parties. It stated that it had temporarily paused the embedded wallet service in response to the issue; however, after an initial investigation, no evidence was found that MetaMask users were impacted.

In his X post, Mishaboar criticized social signing. "Social signing, the feature you may want to add to your wallet if you hate your users," Mishaboar wrote.

Social signing, the feature you may want to add to your wallet if you hate your users. The worst part is that the users that use the social signing option -and which will end up being hacked through it - are also often newbies, entering crypto for the first time. And the risk goes beyond the funds in your wallet - data leaks could link your real life identity to your holdings, which can have terrible consequences.

The concern is particularly significant for inexperienced crypto users who may not recognize the risks associated with connecting their personal accounts to wallet services. While the feature makes wallet creation and access easier, it could introduce security vulnerabilities that users may not fully understand, Mishaboar argued.

"The worst part is that the users that use the social signing option—and who will end up being hacked through it—are also often newbies, entering crypto for the first time. And the risk goes beyond the funds in your wallet—data leaks could link your real-life identity to your holdings, which can have terrible consequences," Mishaboar stated.

Mishaboar noted that this warning also extends to wallets using social sign-in, which allows users to back up their keys in the "Cloud," which just means somebody else's server, he explained.

This week, a security advisory was issued for iOS users, who are urged to update their devices to enhance their wallet security. This follows security researchers identifying two exploit kits, Coruna and DarkSword, which target devices running older iOS versions. These do not rely on a flaw in any wallet app, but once a device is compromised, they can access wallet data stored on it.
